title: Abstract DP168: Chronic Stroke Plasma Triggers Microglial Activation and Cognitive Decline in Young Mice

evidence_spans.quote: Methods: Blood plasma was collected from aged (18-month-old) male and female C57Bl/6 mice
In the brain, stroke plasma caused pronounced microglial activation
Increased gliosis and senescent-like phenotypes were confirmed using immunohistochemistry.
Our ongoing work aims to identify the molecular mediators of these effects through multi-omic profiling.

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This primary mouse experiment analyzes a confirmed senescent-like phenotype. Multi-omic profiling is stated only as ongoing future work; the current report describes flow cytometry and non-omics outcomes.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Retro-orbital infusion of plasma from aged mice in the chronic phase of ischemic stroke
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Recognition and associative memory impairment; microglial activation and related brain inflammatory/senescent markers
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes in young recipient mice infused with chronic stroke plasma versus sham-donor plasma
